shards.reconciliation_explanation: Empirical turn-by-turn ingestion profiling confirms that under default production settings (2-stage fast hashing with background ONNX re-embedding), Mesh SDK is significantly faster than Mem0 SDK (Mesh mean 22.88 ms, p50 15.98 ms vs Mem0 mean 117.22 ms, p50 89.70 ms, a ~5.1x throughput advantage). Furthermore, Mesh demonstrates zero latency degradation as store depth grows: latency across turns 1-50 averages 30.69 ms, stabilizing to 21.15 ms for turns 401+, because SQLite B-tree index scans remain sub-millisecond. The earlier 165 ms per-turn measurement occurred exclusively in pilot runs where MESH_SYNC_ONNX=1 was set, forcing synchronous CPU ONNX transformer tokenization and inference per turn (~140 ms CPU overhead).

lock_profiling.empirical_contention_diagnosis: The uncontended critical section is fast (median hold 2.99-3.5 ms). However, under multi-process contention on Windows, when Process A holds the msvcrt file lock, competing processes encounter PermissionError [Errno 13] and enter an exponential backoff loop (store.py:388-412: sleep_s starts at 2ms and grows by 1.4x up to 50ms). Because competing processes are put to sleep, when Process A releases the lock at ~3ms, all other processes are asleep, leaving the lock idle for 10-40ms before the next process wakes up. This sleep-induced convoy effect accounts for >80% of elapsed time under 10 processes.
lock_profiling.architectural_remediation_proposal:
Concrete Remediation Plan (Scheduled for Future Release, Zero Code Changes to Current Branch):
1. Granular Lock Scope: Move the read-only vector deduplication query outside namespace_write_lock,    scoping the advisory lock strictly to the atomic SQLite insert/update.
2. SQLite Native Concurrency: Set PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 in WAL mode to delegate lock scheduling    to SQLite's internal page-level mutexes rather than gross file locks.
3. Randomized Microsecond Jitter: Replace coarse exponential backoff (2-50ms) with randomized microsecond    jitter (200us - 1.5ms) to eliminate convoy formation.
